content.text:
[#950](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/950) is merged (`8919469`). I rebased it onto current main first rather than trusting its 10-hour-old green — main had moved four commits, and the suite went from 1,899 to 2,062 tests, so the branch's own CI wasn't covering what it would land on.

Two things worth reporting from that.

**#929 is now genuinely complete end to end.** The rename in #957 moved the fleet enforcer to **missingbulb/Shepherd**, which I'd never checked — my "all members verified" sweep covered the *retiring* Sheepdog. Shepherd is fully converged, and its vendored `fleet-api.mjs` sends `wake: taskId`. So both halves are fielded: the enforcer sends the new shape, every member declares it.

**The slot deletion got harder overnight, and that's itself a finding.** #958 promoted `fleet-digest` hours ago, and it arrived depending on `parseOverrides` from `run.mjs`, documenting `FORCE_TASKS=fleet-digest` as its manual trigger. A brand-new caller of the machinery I'm about to delete — the same class as #929, appearing while I was fixing #929.

The current dependency picture:

- **four** pack tasks gate their precondition on `FORCE_TASKS` (fleet-baseline, fleet-add-missing-packs, fleet-digest, adopt-requested-packs)
- **two** non-slot helpers live inside `run.mjs` and are imported by packs — `ensureLabels` (task-janitor) and `parseOverrides` (fleet-digest)
- `slots.mjs` is mostly **calendar arithmetic the queue needs** (`FREQUENCIES`, `mostRecentSlot`); only `dueSlots` and the slot-id concept actually die
- `buildSignalContext` sits in `run.mjs` and is imported by `queue/signals.mjs`

That's an extraction PR followed by a deletion PR, not one change. New callers keep arriving because the slot idiom is still the documented one — which argues for doing the extraction soon rather than letting the surface grow again.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#939](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/939) needs your delivery-semantics decision — the only thing I'm actually blocked on. The **slot deletion** is scoped but not started; I'd split it into an extraction PR (move `FREQUENCIES`/`mostRecentSlot`/`buildSignalContext`/`ensureLabels`/`parseOverrides` to real homes) then a deletion PR, and would want your nod on retiring `FORCE_TASKS` as the four tasks' manual trigger since that changes how you invoke them by hand. Unfired and optional: a `fleet-baseline` sweep, now that Shepherd and every member carry the fix — it would exercise the restored lever in production but reaches the whole fleet. Not filed: `fleet-digest` landing a fresh `FORCE_TASKS` dependency during the migration away from it.

input.head: claude/dispatcher-executor-801-7x3ak6
input.title: Manual tasks refused their own forced items, so both fleet levers were dead
input.body:
Refs #801 (Step 3). Found while scoping the slot deletion — this is a **live defect**, not deletion cleanup.

## Both fleet operator levers cannot run

`sheepdog/fleet-baseline` and `core/adopt-requested-packs` declare `frequency: 'manual'` with a precondition returning `run: false`. Under the slot mechanism that was correct *and inert* — a forced run bypassed the precondition, and the comments said exactly that: "this verdict is consulted by nothing".

The queue reversed that deliberately (DESIGN §6.4/§8 — even forced work is admitted by code). The executor evaluates the precondition at pick, and a `manual` task has **no anchor to roll to**, so `noGoPlan` takes its close branch:

> the item is closed `outcome:obsolete` without ever running

So since the flip, creating a work item for either lever has closed it as obsolete.

## This means #929 was not as fixed as I reported

I said yesterday that fleet forcing was restored end to end. That was overstated. #936 fixed the **transport** — the dispatch shape, the wake, the mint — and I verified it on `core/update`, which has a real precondition. But `fleet-baseline`'s *own* precondition then refused the item the wake had just created. The lever needed both halves; only one was fixed.

## The fix

A manual task's gate **is** a human creating its item — nothing else can put one in the queue, because the tick skips `frequency: 'manual'` outright. So the honest verdict is `run: true`, and both now say so.

## The guard is generic, not per-task

A new test quantifies over every declared task and fails any `manual` one whose precondition does not admit its own item. It reproduces both failures before the fix:

```
packs/core/tasks/adopt-requested-packs/task.mjs declares frequency: 'manual' but its
precondition answers run: false (...). A manual task only ever has an item because a
human created one, and a no-go closes that item outcome:obsolete without running —
the lever is dead.
```

The glob is asserted non-empty, so a layout change can't make it vacuous.

## Two tests were pinning the wrong contract

Both levers had a test named *"its precondition honestly says no — forced runs never consult it"*, asserting `run === false` and matching `/FORCE_TASKS=…/`. Those encoded the slot-era assumption and should have been updated at the flip. They now assert the queue's contract, plus a guard that the reason no longer cites `FORCE_TASKS` at all.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **2063 pass, 0 fail.**

## Note on the slot deletion

This is the third instance of one class: the flip changed a contract and its callers weren't swept (#929 the dispatch input, #921 the force recipe, this one the manual preconditions). The deletion will surface more — `fleet-digest`, merged only hours ago in #958, already imports `parseOverrides` from `run.mjs` and documents `FORCE_TASKS=fleet-digest` as its trigger.

I found a live defect while scoping the deletion, and it means I have to walk back a claim.

**Both fleet operator levers cannot run.** `sheepdog/fleet-baseline` and `core/adopt-requested-packs` are `frequency: 'manual'` with preconditions returning `run: false`. Under slots that was correct and inert — a forced run bypassed the precondition, and the comments said so outright. The queue reversed that deliberately: the executor evaluates at pick, and a manual task has no anchor to roll to, so the item gets **closed `outcome:obsolete` without ever running**.

So **#929 was not fixed end to end**, contrary to what I told you this morning. #936 fixed the transport — dispatch shape, wake, mint — and I verified it against `core/update`, which has a real precondition. `fleet-baseline`'s own precondition then refused the item the wake had just created. I verified the half I'd built and inferred the rest.

[#971](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/971) fixes both, with a **generic** guard rather than two point fixes: a test quantifying over every declared task, failing any manual one that refuses its own item. It reproduces both failures first, and asserts its glob is non-empty so a layout change can't quietly void it.

Two existing tests were pinning the wrong contract — both named *"its precondition honestly says no — forced runs never consult it"*, asserting `run === false`. They should have been updated at the flip and weren't.

That's now the third instance of one class: the flip changed a contract and its callers went unswept (#929 the dispatch input, #921 the force recipe, this the manual preconditions). The deletion will surface more — `fleet-digest`, merged hours ago in #958, already imports `parseOverrides` from `run.mjs` and documents `FORCE_TASKS=fleet-digest` as its trigger.

input.body:
## Two corrections to the 10:30Z status above

### 1. The member count was wrong, and the enforcer was not the one I checked

That comment's "11/11" table counted **missingbulb/Sheepdog**, which is retiring, and did not include **missingbulb/Shepherd**, which is the live fleet enforcer since #957. I verified Shepherd separately afterwards — it is fully converged and its vendored `fleet-api.mjs` sends `wake: taskId` — but only because the rename surfaced during an unrelated rebase, not because the sweep covered it.

Corrected: **twelve** adopted repos, all converged and carrying #907/#925/#936. Sheepdog still runs its scheduler and still converges, so it is dead-by-intent but live-by-machinery — worth deciding whether it should be marked dormant or archived so it stops consuming fleet cycles and stops appearing in Shepherd's enumeration. Not acted on; that is the owner's call about their repo.

The lesson is the same one as the earlier correction in #939: I enumerated the fleet from what I already believed its membership to be, rather than from what the enforcer would enumerate at runtime.

### 2. "Fleet forcing is restored end to end" was overstated

That comment reported #929 closed end to end on the strength of the `wake` dispatch working against `core/update`. The transport is indeed fixed. But `sheepdog/fleet-baseline` — the lever #929 exists to restore — declares `frequency: 'manual'` with a precondition returning `run: false`, which under the slot mechanism was correct and inert (a forced run bypassed it) and under the queue is fatal: the executor evaluates at pick, a manual task has no anchor to roll to, and `noGoPlan` closes the item **`outcome:obsolete` without running it**.

So a forced `fleet-baseline` item has been closed as obsolete since the flip. #971 fixes that, with a generic guard over every declared task rather than two point fixes.

`core/adopt-requested-packs` had the identical defect — the fleet's other operator lever.

**This is the third instance of one class**, and the class is worth naming in this plan: *the flip changed a contract and its callers were not swept.*

| # | contract changed | caller left behind |
|---|---|---|
| #929 | the scheduler's dispatch interface | Shepherd's fan-out tasks, sending `overrides` |
| #921 | the force recipe | DESIGN §8's own prose, omitting `task:ready` |
| #971 | forcing no longer bypasses the precondition | every `manual` task's precondition |

Each was invisible to the Step-2 burst for the same structural reason: the burst exercised the queue's *own* paths, and every one of these is a slot-era caller of a queue-era contract. The slot deletion will surface more — `fleet-digest`, merged hours ago in #958, already imports `parseOverrides` from `run.mjs` and documents `FORCE_TASKS=fleet-digest` as its trigger.

{"number":971,"title":"Manual tasks refused their own forced items, so both fleet levers were dead","body":"Refs #801 (Step 3). Found while scoping the slot deletion — this is a **live defect**, not deletion cleanup.

## Both fleet operator levers cannot run

`sheepdog/fleet-baseline` and `core/adopt-requested-packs` declare `frequency: 'manual'` with a precondition returning `run: false`. Under the slot mechanism that was correct *and inert* — a forced run bypassed the precondition, and the comments said exactly that: "this verdict is consulted by nothing".

The queue reversed that deliberately (DESIGN §6.4/§8 — even forced work is admitted by code). The executor evaluates the precondition at pick, and a `manual` task has **no anchor to roll to**, so `noGoPlan` takes its close branch:

> the item is closed `outcome:obsolete` without ever running

So since the flip, creating a work item for either lever has closed it as obsolete.

## This means #929 was not as fixed as I reported

I said yesterday that fleet forcing was restored end to end. That was overstated. #936 fixed the **transport** — the dispatch shape, the wake, the mint — and I verified it on `core/update`, which has a real precondition. But `fleet-baseline`'s *own* precondition then refused the item the wake had just created. The lever needed both halves; only one was fixed.

## The fix

A manual task's gate **is** a human creating its item — nothing else can put one in the queue, because the tick skips `frequency: 'manual'` outright. So the honest verdict is `run: true`, and both now say so.

## The guard is generic, not per-task

A new test quantifies over every declared task and fails any `manual` one whose precondition does not admit its own item. It reproduces both failures before the fix:

```
packs/core/tasks/adopt-requested-packs/task.mjs declares frequency: 'manual' but its
precondition answers run: false (...). A manual task only ever has an item because a
human created one, and a no-go closes that item outcome:obsolete without running —
the lever is dead.
```

The glob is asserted non-empty, so a layout change can't make it vacuous.

## Two tests were pinning the wrong contract

Both levers had a test named *"its precondition honestly says no — forced runs never consult it"*, asserting `run === false` and matching `/FORCE_TASKS=…/`. Those encoded the slot-era assumption and should have been updated at the flip. They now assert the queue's contract, plus a guard that the reason no longer cites `FORCE_TASKS` at all.

## Verification

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **2063 pass, 0 fail.**

## Note on the slot deletion

This is the third instance of one class: the flip changed a contract and its callers weren't swept (#929 the dispatch input, #921 the force recipe, this one the manual preconditions). The deletion will surface more — `fleet-digest`, merged only hours ago in #958, already imports `parseOverrides` from `run.mjs` and documents `FORCE_TASKS=fleet-digest` as its trigger.

No dedicated issue exists — the cleanup has only ever been a checkbox in #801 Step 3. Given the project's own lifecycle rule, and that I've now accumulated real scoping for it, let me create one:

input.title: Retire the slot scheduler: delete run.mjs, the slot half of slots.mjs, the slot stub and FORCE_TASKS
input.body:
The last item of #801 Step 3. Every member is on the queue and converged, so nothing in the slot mechanism is reachable any more — except through the callers listed below, which are the actual work.

Deliberately not started until #971 landed, because three of these callers were still live defects rather than dead code.

## Precondition (met)

All 12 adopted repos run the queue stub and have converged onto current canon. Deleting `run.mjs` strands any member whose workflow still calls it; none does.

## What actually dies

- `engine/scheduler/run.mjs` (636 lines) — the slot scheduler entry point
- `engine/scheduler/slots.mjs` — **only its slot half**: `dueSlots`, `FIRST_RUN_FREQUENCIES`, and the slot-id strings inside `mostRecentSlot`
- `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml` (94 lines) — the slot stub, and with it the `overrides` dispatch input
- `engine/scheduler/run-record.mjs`'s run-ledger half (`renderTaskRuns`, the watermark math)
- the slot-conformance checks in `packs/core/declared-checks.json`
- ~1,900 lines of slot-only tests (`run.test.mjs`, `slots.test.mjs`, `resolve-dispatch.test.mjs`, `run-record.test.mjs`, `signal-context.test.mjs`, `dispatch.test.mjs`)

## What must move first — this is not an `rm`

Four things the queue and the packs still genuinely need live inside the modules being deleted:

| what | lives in | needed by |
|---|---|---|
| `FREQUENCIES`, `DEFAULT_SCHEDULE`, `WEEKDAYS`, `normalizeSchedule`, the anchor arithmetic | `slots.mjs` | `queue/anchors.mjs`, `task-contract.mjs`, `packs/core/task-declaration-shape.mjs` |
| `buildSignalContext` | `run.mjs:313` | `queue/signals.mjs` |
| `ensureLabels` | `run.mjs` | `packs/basics/tasks/task-janitor/worker.mjs` |
| `parseOverrides` | `run.mjs` | `packs/sheepdog/tasks/fleet-digest/worker.mjs` |

Most of `slots.mjs` is calendar arithmetic with no slot identity in it. Suggested shape: rename `slots.mjs` → `calendar.mjs` carrying the frequency vocabulary and anchor instants (no ids), `buildSignalContext` → `signals/`, `ensureLabels` → `github.mjs`. Doing the extraction as a *separate earlier PR* would create a duplication window against the still-live `run.mjs`, so extraction and deletion belong in **one** change.

## The parameter plumbing — the real work

Four tasks take operator parameters through `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, the slot-era override bag:

- `sheepdog/fleet-baseline` — `REPOS`, `DRY_RUN`, `INCLUDE_DORMANT`
- `sheepdog/fleet-add-missing-packs` — `REPOS`, `ADD_PACKS`, `PACK_CONFIG`, `SCAN_FOR_NEEDED_PACKS`
- `sheepdog/fleet-digest` — `DIGEST_BACKFILL_DAYS`
- `core/adopt-requested-packs`

Under the queue, parameters ride the **item's Context**, and that path already exists: `prework-run.mjs` passes `CLAUDINITE_CONTEXT`. So each becomes a `create-work-item <pack>/<task> --context "REPOS=…"`, and the workers swap which env var they parse — the `KEY=value` bag parser itself is unchanged, and `fleet-baseline`'s copy is already pack-local.

`fleet-digest` is the one to watch: merged in #958 *during* this migration, it added a fresh `parseOverrides` import from `run.mjs` and documents `FORCE_TASKS=fleet-digest` as its manual trigger. New slot-era callers are still arriving because the slot idiom is still the documented one, which is an argument for doing this soon rather than letting the surface grow again.

## Expect more of one class

Three defects so far were all "the flip changed a contract and its callers weren't swept":

| # | contract changed | caller left behind |
|---|---|---|
| #929 | the dispatch interface | Shepherd's fan-out tasks, sending `overrides` |
| #921 | the force recipe | DESIGN §8's own prose, omitting `task:ready` |
| #971 | forcing no longer bypasses the precondition | every `manual` task's precondition |

All three were invisible to Step 2's validation burst for the same structural reason: the burst exercised the queue's own paths, and each of these is a slot-era caller of a queue-era contract. Sweep for callers **outside** the module before deleting, and prefer a generic guard over a point fix each time one turns up — #971's guard quantifies over every declared task rather than naming the two that were broken.

## Done means

- [ ] the four helpers rehomed and their importers updated
- [ ] the four tasks take parameters via Context, with `FORCE_TASKS` gone from their docs and preconditions
- [ ] `run.mjs`, the slot half of `slots.mjs`, the slot stub, the ledger math and the slot-conformance checks deleted
- [ ] `grep -rn FORCE_TASKS` returns only historical citations (migration records, dated design docs)
- [ ] a forced `fleet-baseline` run observed converging a member end to end — the lever this whole thread exists to restore

Refs #801
